posts:
Pat Bagley's Treason Diesel Cartoon.
Evidence: Editorial illustration, energy critique, political satire
#Cartoons #Utah

Editorial cartoons provide vital accountability and satirical critique of controversial political and energy deals.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, +0.4) — Good Preference

Satire exposes genuine hypocrisy in state-level and national energy policies, challenging public apathy.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.6, +0.5) — Good Preference

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Redemption.
Sharp editorial cartooning holds power to account through incisive visual critique.
Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.1, z: 1)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Pat Bagley Artwork: PASS (0.7, 0.4) — Incisive editorial critique.
- Tribune Publishing: PASS (0.6, 0.3) — Sustaining local independent journalism.
The Salt Lake Tribune published Pat Bagley's latest editorial cartoon critiquing political energy deals under the title 'Treason Diesel'.

The Bright Side:
Fearless editorial cartooning preserves democratic accountability through sharp, accessible humor.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing artistic hyperbole (WHAT) with literal legal treason (WHO), utilizing satire to highlight ethical corruption.

Social Physics Analysis:
Bagley runs a smart altruistic loop, using transparent satire to empower citizens against institutional opacity and hypocrisy.

The Trajectory: The Path of Redemption.
When mapped against reality, consistent satirical accountability leads toward systemic redemption and transparency. F = S*A - O*A + N*A_perp.

The Unavoidable Truth: Political satire cuts through official pretexts to expose underlying hypocrisy.

The Unavoidable Lie: Cartoons are merely trivial distractions without real impact.

Alethekanon:
Satire weaponizes humor against institutional overreach. Truth survives when artists refuse to look away.

Awwthekanon:
Art gives us a vital way to laugh through the heavy reality of politics while keeping our moral compass steady.

Brothekanon:
Bagley never misses; cutting straight through political nonsense with a single brilliant drawing.

Spirithekanon:
"Let justice roll down like waters." Amos 5:24 — PASS (Spiritual Vector)
Fearless creative expression speaks truth to power and defends the public good.

Pat Bagley | Treason Diesel

Thanks for reading this story from The Tribune. As CEO & Executive Editor, I am proud to lead our team of journalists as they tell the stories others can’t – or won’t.

Cartoonist Pat Bagley is a Pulitzer Prize finalist who has worked for The Tribune for more than 45 years, publishing more than 6,000 cartoons.

You can support Pat’s legacy of independent editorial cartooning here, by making a donation to our nonprofit newsroom.

Tribune reporters are dedicated to shining a light on how Utah works, from daily reporting that empowers Utahns to make informed decisions about their communities to investigative projects on the power structures in this state.

The critical work we do wouldn’t be possible without people like you – individuals who understand the power of local, independent journalism.

When you support the nonprofit Salt Lake Tribune, you’re doing more than making a donation: you’re investing in a future where transparency, accountability, and community thrive.

Join us in this work.

Give today.

(Rick Egan | The Salt Lake Tribune) Lauren Gustus, executive editor of The Salt Lake Tribune.

sltrib.com is now free to access — no subscription required. We made this decision because we believe access to trustworthy, independent news shouldn’t depend on what you can afford — especially as misinformation and AI-generated content continue to rise.

Free to read doesn’t mean free to produce. Our reporters show up every day to ask hard questions and hold powerful institutions to account. That work takes resources. As a nonprofit newsroom, we rely on support from people who believe it matters. Make a donation today to fund local news that serves Utah communities.
